title: An RDMA-First Object Storage System with SmartNIC Offload (ROS2)
event_hint: A DPU/SmartNIC-offloaded, RDMA-first object storage design (ROS2) that moves the DAOS client onto an NVIDIA BlueField-3, removing host mediation from the data path for GPU-centric AI training/inference I/O.
problem: AI training and inference impose sustained, fine-grain I/O that stresses host-mediated, TCP-based storage paths, creating a host-CPU bottleneck and limiting data delivery to GPU-centric pipelines.
mechanism: RDMA-first object storage: offloads the DAOS client to an NVIDIA BlueField-3 SmartNIC (DPU); separates a lightweight gRPC control plane (namespace + capability exchange) from a high-throughput RDMA/TCP data plane (UCX/libfabric); removes host mediation from the data path entirely, enabling DPU-resident multi-tenant isolation and inline services (e.g., encryption/decryption).

evidence.claim: On server-grade CPUs, RDMA consistently outperforms TCP for both large sequential and small random I/O.
When the RDMA-driven DAOS client is offloaded to BlueField-3, end-to-end performance is comparable to the host.
TCP on the SmartNIC lags host performance, underscoring the importance of RDMA for offloaded deployments.
SmartNIC offload preserves RDMA efficiency while enabling DPU-resident features such as multi-tenant isolation and inline encryption/decryption.

evaluation_context: Evaluated with FIO/DFS across local and remote configurations on server-grade CPUs and NVIDIA BlueField-3. Abstract reports relative comparisons only; no absolute throughput or latency numbers.
limitations: Abstract-level evidence only; no specific throughput/latency numbers, model sizes, or GPU-direct results in the abstract. GPU-direct placement for LLM tasks is explicitly future work. Full paper body not fetched.
project_relevance: Core fit for the DPU/SmartNIC-offload briefing track: demonstrates that a SmartNIC-offloaded, RDMA-first data plane can match host performance while moving isolation and inline crypto onto the DPU. Relevant pattern transfer to KVCache cross-node transfer (RDMA-first data plane separated from control plane) and to TPN inference-network I/O where host mediation is the bottleneck.
